title: add-vpc-control-plane-provisioning-subnets-endpoints-security-groups-peering-dns
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: enable automated provisioning of the Private Control Plane VPC resources for on-prem/VPC deployments. This PR extends the private-installer terraform modules and helm hooks to create a VPC control plane stack that includes multi-az subnets, necessary interface and gateway endpoints, security group rules for control-plane components, cross-account VPC peering configuration, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation for service discovery.

What changed: added a new terraform module modules/vpc-control-plane which composes subnets, route tables, interface/gateway endpoints (S3, STS, EC2), security groups tuned for control plane traffic (k8s api, webhook, etcd-like traffic for state sync), and peering resources with optional cross-account permissions. Also added optional route53 delegation and managed zone resources for private DNS to enable control-plane DNS entries to resolve across peered VPCs. The installer was updated to expose high-level flags: enable_control_plane_vpc, control_plane_az_count, create_endpoints, peer_account_ids, and private_dns_delegation. Helm chart hooks now include a pre-install job that validates DNS delegation and exports the generated kubeconfig for the control-plane operator.

Compatibility and migration: the changes are additive and opt-in by default. Existing customers who do not enable enable_control_plane_vpc are unaffected. For upgrades where customers previously managed their VPCs, a migration guide was added describing how to switch from manual VPC wiring to the new automated flow with minimal downtime (create peering, validate DNS, cutover).

Testing: module unit tests (terraform validate/plan with local mocked variables) and end-to-end smoke in our integration harness were run. Ran installer on a staging account with 3 AZs and validated cross-account peering + DNS resolution across peered VPCs. CI: full terraform lint/plan/test and helm lint passed.

Notes on security: security group defaults are conservative; we explicitly document required CIDR blocks and provide an allowlist for operator IPs. Peering resources can be created without full cross-account acceptance when using the peer_account_ids flow; otherwise operators must accept the peering request via the console or automation documented in the upgrade notes.
commits: feat(terraform): add modules/vpc-control-plane with subnets, route tables, endpoints
chore(helm): add pre-install DNS validation job and kubeconfig exporter
test(terraform): add plan-based unit tests for control plane module
fix(security): tighten sg rules and document operator allowlist
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Please verify cross-account IAM policy implications for the peering module - added comments and explicit policy docs in modules/vpc-control-plane/README.md

Hannah Lee: Can we limit the number of created endpoints by default? Response: default is create_endpoints = false; installer sets it to true only when enable_control_plane_vpc=true and --create-endpoints flag passed during install. Tests updated to cover both flows.

Marcus Chen: Suggest tightening SG egress to only required AWS services (S3/STS). Response: updated sg rules and added explicit egress allowlist controlled by variable control_plane_allowed_egress_services.
QA: Ran e2e in staging and reported a DNS propagation delay edge case - added retry logic in pre-install job and documented expected propagation time in README.
ci_summary: ci/terraform-plan-control-plane: passed, ci/helm-lint-and-test: passed, unit-tests: passed, integration-smoke: passed
release_notes: Added opt-in automated provisioning for Private Control Plane VPC resources: multi-AZ subnets, interface/gateway endpoints, security groups, optional cross-account peering, and Route53 private DNS delegation. Installer flags and migration guide included.
